rubric_items.reason: All 15 known REQs are traced; REQ-11 now also covers the patient page via S-7 (previous F-1 addressed for the patient page).
Stories mostly carry one outcome; S-5 still bundles label, filter and dashboard constraint but stays small.
S-1/S-2/S-4 bracket 24h at 09:59/10:01 and discriminate well, but S-7 AC1 expects a Stale (past, non-Scheduled) appointment in the doctor page table, which lists only upcoming Scheduled ones.
24h comes from REQ-2/A-02 and the one-minute offsets are derived inline; dates are example data, not limits.
Terms are consistent with the glossary and intent; S-6 title is still a documentation task rather than a user-facing outcome.

findings.text: S-7 AC1 expects the doctor page to list a Stale appointment, but that table shows only upcoming Scheduled appointments (status SCHEDULED, starts_at >= now). A Stale one is past and not Scheduled, so it never appears; the AC silently widens REQ-11 ('shown today').

cites.quote: when staff open that doctor's page, then the appointments table shows Stale for the Stale one
wherever an appointment status is shown today

findings.suggested_fix: Drop S-7 AC1 and note, as done for the dashboard (C8), that the doctor page lists only upcoming Scheduled appointments, so a Stale one never appears there; keep the patient-page AC2.

findings.text: Previous F-2 still open: S-6's title describes a documentation change, not an outcome a user sees.
findings.suggested_fix: Retitle as a reader outcome, for example 'Staff can look up what Stale means in the glossary'.
